prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Evidence is still thin for adoption redesign, finish new_screen, finish notification, and sign_in reorder, as each has only one test.
No clear effect was seen for choose_path copy across 2 tests; despite leaning positive, neither test was statistically significant.
No clear effect was seen for home wait_info across 2 tests.
No kind of change can be called helpful yet, as no test achieved a statistically significant win.
Predictions were overly optimistic in round 1, but underestimated measured outcomes in round 2 when predicting lower or negative gains.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, redesign: -2.8% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- choose_path, copy: +1.1% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- finish, new_screen: +2.1% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, notification: +2.0% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- home, wait_info: -0.9% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- sign_in, reorder: +0.4% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 72.9%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 17.8%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [adoption, redesign] Companion Archetype Trait Selection: Redesigns the friend selection screen into a split visual archetype layout where users select pet personality traits alongside visual styles. (why: Adoption has a low 60.9% conversion and long median completion time (89s), while custom pet generation results trigger user complaints.)
1: [home, new_flow] Visual Stage Hatching Sequence: Rebuilds the waiting step into a staged visual journey displaying companion creation milestones as the pet comes to life. (why: The waiting step has a high mean duration (2336s) and 81.3% conversion, suggesting users leave or stall while awaiting generation.)
2: [sign_in, reorder] Post-Certificate Account Registration: Moves sign-in screen to occur immediately after adoption certificate completion before desktop rendering begins. (why: 8 support tickets mention missing pets after re-login; registering right after finalizing the pet certificate ensures immediate account binding.)
3: [sign_in, hint] Account Pet-Link Reassurance Hint: Adds an explicit security hint on the sign-in screen confirming that account login permanently saves created desktop pets. (why: 8 support emails complained about missing or reset pets after signing in again.)
4: [home, wait_info] Desktop Diagnostic Rendering Status: Displays real-time technical status updates on the waiting screen showing display driver and desktop integration steps. (why: 3 support tickets reported pet failing to appear on desktop or app failing to open during initial setup.)
5: [finish, notification] Background Rendering System Notification: Adds desktop system notification prompt alerting users when background pet asset rendering finishes. (why: Finish step mean time is extremely long (5815s), showing users switch to other apps while setup completes.)
6: [choose_path, copy] Path Differentiation Value Copy: Clarifies the path options by contrasting instant pre-built companion adoption against custom AI pet creation. (why: choose_path conversion is 76.2% with a long mean duration of 514s, indicating initial user hesitation.)
